subject: Approval request: one-time credit for Northwind Analytics (confirmed metering defect)
body:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwoodinference.com>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Feb 6, 2026 at 9:14 AM PT
Subject: Approval request: one-time credit for Northwind Analytics (confirmed metering defect)

Laura — requesting CFO approval for a one-time credit for Northwind Analytics due to a confirmed metering defect (streaming disconnect accounting) impacting a subset of their January usage.

Summary
- Customer: Northwind Analytics (Hosted API)
- Issue: tokens after client disconnect were incorrectly counted as billable in some cases (confirmed via reconciliation + log review)
- Affected window: 2026-01-13 through 2026-01-22 (UTC)
- Scope: streaming responses on /v1/chat/completions for model alias rw-open-llama-70b (plus small spillover on rw-mixtral-8x7b)

Quantified exposure (Northwind)
- Invoice delta attributable to defect: $18,430 (approx. 7.1% of Jan usage charges)
- Recommended credit: $18,430 applied as a line-item credit memo against Feb invoice (or a one-time service credit if they prefer)
- Method: replay sample of affected request_ids, apply corrected billing rules (bill only tokens actually delivered before disconnect), scale to full population by request count; results align with the daily aggregate delta distribution for that window.

Wider exposure (for awareness)
- We’ve identified 3 additional accounts with smaller deltas in the same window; combined estimated exposure across all affected accounts: $41–48k.
- We are not proactively issuing credits unless a customer disputes; however, for Northwind we have an active complaint and need to respond within their procurement timeline.

Proposed controls / prevention
- Engineering fix is in review (see Ethan’s status), with targeted backfill for the affected window.
- Add a pre-invoice meter health check and daily reconciliation job (per-dimension deltas + alerting to #finance and SRE).
- Update dispute runbook language + internal FAQ for Support/Sales so we explain the root cause consistently.

Decision needed
- Approve $18,430 credit (Northwind) today so we can close out the case and send a written response.

Attachments:
- Northwind_metering_defect_exposure_2026-02-06.xlsx
- Draft_customer_note_Northwind_credit_2026-02-06.docx

Thanks,
Rishi

—
Rishi Malhotra
FP&A / Unit Economics
Redwood Inference


From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwoodinference.com>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Feb 6, 2026 at 9:38 AM PT
Subject: Re: Approval request: one-time credit for Northwind Analytics (confirmed metering defect)

A few questions before I approve:

1) Confidence: how tight is the estimate for Northwind? (i.e., are we sure the $18.4k isn’t a range?)
2) Fix + backfill: when will corrected aggregates be in place and how will we prevent this from reappearing?
3) Customer comms: does the draft note admit “overbilling” explicitly? I want to avoid language that invites broad audit requests.

Also, please confirm whether we need to hold any invoices or if this is isolated to January streaming in that window.

Laura

—
Laura Bennett
CFO
Redwood Inference


From: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Feb 6, 2026 at 10:12 AM PT
Subject: Re: Approval request: one-time credit for Northwind Analytics (confirmed metering defect)

Jumping in on (2).

Root cause
- In the streaming path, we were not consistently applying the “client disconnected” flag before final token aggregation.
- Net effect: some completion tokens generated after disconnect were included in billable output_tokens.

Status / fix
- PR redwood/pr_41903 corrects disconnect handling so we only bill tokens actually delivered before the stream terminates.
- We added regression tests covering:
  - client disconnect mid-stream
  - partial chunk delivery
  - retry + reconnect behavior (ensuring we don’t double-count)

Backfill / auditability
- We can backfill the affected window (Jan 13–22 UTC) once the fix is deployed. Plan is to regenerate billing aggregates for that window using the corrected logic and compare deltas against invoiced totals.
- We’ll produce an audit evidence bundle: before/after aggregates + query links + invoice_run_id mapping.

Prevention
- In parallel, ENG-4821 adds daily reconciliation and alerting (dimension-level diffs). SRE asked for suppression rules during backfills to avoid false positives, but alerts will be on by default.

Scope
- Based on the log query we ran, it’s isolated to streaming endpoints in that time window. Non-streaming requests are unaffected.
- No need to hold broader invoicing; we can handle Northwind via credit while we backfill and confirm other accounts.

Ethan

—
Ethan Park
Platform Engineering (Control Plane)
Redwood Inference


From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Feb 6, 2026 at 11:03 AM PT
Subject: Re: Approval request: one-time credit for Northwind Analytics (confirmed metering defect)

On (3): I reviewed the draft note.

Suggested framing (to reduce audit risk while being transparent):
- Acknowledge “billing discrepancy due to a metering issue in streaming disconnect handling” rather than “overbilling.”
- Confirm we validated the impact for their account and are issuing a credit for the affected amount.
- State that the issue is remediated and that we have added monitoring/reconciliation controls.
- Avoid broad statements about “all customers” or “all invoices” until we complete the backfill analysis.

Also recommend we keep the credit as a credit memo/service credit applied to the next invoice unless they specifically request a refund. (If they request a refund, we can reassess, but credit is cleaner operationally.)

Michael

—
Michael Grant
General Counsel
Redwood Inference


From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwoodinference.com>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Feb 6, 2026 at 12:37 PM PT
Subject: Re: Approval request: one-time credit for Northwind Analytics (confirmed metering defect)

Approved to issue a one-time credit memo for Northwind Analytics in the amount of $18,430, contingent on the following:

- Update the customer note per Michael’s guidance (use “billing discrepancy / metering issue,” confirm credit amount, confirm remediation + controls).
- Ensure we capture an internal postmortem summary (1-pager) with: impacted window, detection, root cause, and controls (daily recon + pre-invoice checks).
- Confirm the backfill results for the broader population and send me a short update by end of next week with final exposure and any additional customer action needed.

Rishi: please coordinate with billing ops to apply the credit to Feb invoice and close the loop with Support. Ethan: proceed with the fix/backfill plan and make sure Finance gets the audit evidence artifacts.

Laura

—
Laura Bennett
CFO
Redwood Inference
